key_insight: Video autoencoders are not just compression tools: they shape both the computational cost and responsiveness of interactive world models. Autoencoders designed for offline video generation may not suit systems where agents or humans need immediate feedback.
problem_solved: Interactive world models often reuse text-to-video autoencoders designed without real-time control requirements, potentially creating a mismatch between video compression and action responsiveness.
method: Reconsider video autoencoder design around interactive simulation rather than offline video generation.
Examine compression in terms of per-frame computation and the delay before actions affect generated frames.
The supplied abstract is truncated; specific architectures, training procedures, and experimental results are unavailable.
impact: For practitioners building learned simulators, autoencoder choice is a system-level decision affecting speed and control responsiveness—not merely reconstruction quality.

paper_title: Rethinking Video Autoencoders for Interactive World Models
paper_authors: Adrien Ramanana Rahary, Yutong Bai, Nicolas Dufour, Patrick Pérez, David Picard
